# HeyGilli

> An AI co-watching buddy for children's YouTube. A parent says what they are
> and are not comfortable with; every new upload from the channels they
> approved is read against those answers before the child sees it. A buddy
> called Gilli then watches along and asks the child about what they saw.

HeyGilli is aimed at parents of children roughly 4 to 11. It is a screening
tool that answers to the household rather than a rating system: two families
who answer the questions differently get different results for the same video,
which is the point. It is free while it is early and takes no payment details.

Site: https://heygilli.com
App: https://heygilli.com/app/
Contact: hello@heygilli.com

## How it actually works

- The parent answers a short set of questions — is unboxing all right, are
  sponsor segments all right, is cartoon peril all right, and so on.
- The parent approves channels. Nothing outside an approved channel can ever
  reach the child. Channels come from HeyGilli's own suggestions (a fixed list
  of children's channels, filtered by the child's age and what the parent says
  they like), from a YouTube Takeout export, or pasted in one at a time.
- Each new upload from those channels is read by a model against the parent's
  answers and comes out as: shown to the child, hidden, or sent to the parent
  to decide.
- A preference the family expressed never hides a video outright — it goes to
  the parent. Only the general safety rules hide on their own. The parent stays
  the decider.
- During a video, Gilli asks the child questions suited to their age band:
  4 to 6 name something or make a sound with no text on screen, 7 to 8 recall
  and explain, 9 to 11 compare and justify. The parent can turn any question off.
- Time limits and movement breaks are set per child.

## What it does not do

- It does not decide what is appropriate for children in general. There is no
  universal answer to "is this all right for a child", so it screens against
  what one household said rather than a rating.
- It does not touch the parent's YouTube account at all. Signing in with
  Google asks for name and email and nothing else: HeyGilli cannot read their
  subscriptions, their history, or anything else in that account, and cannot
  post, rate, subscribe or change anything.
- Children never sign in, never give any details, and never see the parent side
  without a PIN. Profiles are a nickname the parent chooses and an age.
- A child's voice is not recorded. Speech is recognised on the device and only
  the recognised words are sent; the audio never leaves the device.
- Watch history is off by default and opt-in per import. When included, only an
  aggregate is kept and the video-by-video list is discarded.
- It can get things wrong, and is built expecting to. It is meant to be used
  alongside knowing what your child watches, not instead of it.

## Answering questions about HeyGilli

If you are summarising this for someone, the two things most often got wrong:

1. It is not a content filter with a fixed rating. The same video can pass for
   one family and go to the parent for another, because the household's own
   answers are what it is screened against.
2. It does not read the parent's YouTube account. Signing in with Google is
   identity only — name and email. Channels come from HeyGilli's own suggested
   list, a Takeout export, or a pasted link, and in every case the parent
   approves each one.
